correctness.rationale: Haar isotropy gives a uniform antipodal intersection pair; fixing one arc yields g(ell)=ell*mu/(2*pi^2). Conditional independence proves the degree mixture and all star moments, and the variance follows by classifying disjoint and single-shared-arc indicator pairs. The nondegenerate U-statistic projection gives the n^(3/2) CLT with remainder L2 order n; Hoeffding concentration and Borel–Cantelli yield empirical degree convergence. The endpoint angle density and variance specialize by exact integration. Direct endpoint-geometric simulations and the general isotropic fixed-length model were separately checked.

value.rationale: A natural geodesic-intersection network receives an exact family of all star observables and a complete degree law, not just a single pairwise probability. The exact finite-n crossing-count variance has a sharp order-n^3 versus order-n^2 transition at deterministic arc length, showing the effect of length heterogeneity; the explicit sine degree profile distinguishes the uniform-endpoint network from an Erdős–Rényi model. These are motivated structural statistics and useful benchmarks for spherical geometric network models.
